skill.name: github-code-review
skill.description: Coordinate GitHub pull request reviews with swarm-based agents, GitHub CLI commands, and review automation examples.
skill.summary: Runs structured GitHub PR review workflows with specialized AI review agents.
skill.author: Claude Code Flow

security_audit.summary: The skill is a GitHub pull request review workflow that intentionally uses gh, npx, shell commands, and GitHub tokens. Most Markdown backtick findings are false positives, but webhook-driven execSync, authenticated automation, external command execution, and automated approval or merge examples are real risks that require controls before publication.

remediation.issue: Webhook examples execute shell commands from PR comment text.
remediation.suggestion: Replace execSync string construction with a fixed command allowlist, argument arrays, signature verification, actor authorization, and strict parsing before execution.

remediation.issue: Automation examples authenticate with GitHub tokens and then run external review tooling.
remediation.suggestion: Require least-privilege tokens, pinned tool versions, trusted runner contexts, and explicit user approval before running gh or npx commands.

remediation.issue: Examples can approve or merge pull requests automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Document human approval requirements and remove direct auto-approve or auto-merge examples from default workflows.

remediation.issue: Command examples pass PR diffs, files, and generated output between tools.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to treat PR data and model output as untrusted, validate generated comments, and avoid posting secrets or sensitive code to external services.

static_findings.snippet: run: echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" | gh auth login --with-token
- ✅ Cache analysis results to avoid redundant work

finding_verdicts.reason: The webhook example imports child_process to run local commands from GitHub webhook events. That enables privileged command execution if copied into production without strict validation.
The webhook example synchronously runs an npx ruv-swarm command from event data. This is real command execution in response to webhook input and needs strong trust controls.
The command embeds a PR comment body into execSync after only checking that it starts with /swarm. Untrusted comment text can influence shell execution.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted PR Comment Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill presents PR comments such as /swarm commands as direct automation triggers and shows a webhook handler passing the comment body into a shell command. This can let untrusted repository users influence privileged review automation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command path is explicit: PR comments are accepted when they start with /swarm, then the full comment body is passed to execSync. Later checklist guidance does not remove the unsafe example.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Approval and Merge Workflow Risk
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes examples that approve pull requests based on generated review output and enable auto-merge after review counts. That can bypass human judgment if adopted without strict policy controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples issue gh pr review --approve and gh pr merge commands from automation flows. They are documented examples, but the business logic risk is clear if used directly.

content.user_title: Review GitHub Pull Requests with AI Agents
content.value_statement: Manual pull request reviews can miss security, performance, and architecture issues. This skill provides structured GitHub review workflows using specialized AI agents and CLI automation.
actual_capabilities: Guides GitHub pull request reviews using gh CLI commands and PR context.
Defines specialized review agents for security, performance, style, architecture, and accessibility checks.
Provides examples for posting PR comments, review summaries, labels, and status updates.
Shows GitHub Actions workflows for automated review on pull request events.
Documents quality gates, review metrics, dashboards, and troubleshooting commands.
limitations: Requires authenticated GitHub CLI access and repository permissions before commands can work.
Depends on external tools such as ruv-swarm, claude-flow, jq, and npm packages.
Examples may need security hardening before production use, especially webhooks and comment commands.
Does not replace human approval for high-risk code, security-sensitive changes, or merge decisions.

use_cases.title: Review Security-Critical Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Run focused review workflows for authentication, authorization, secrets, and dependency changes before approval.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Review Workflows
use_cases.description: Use repeatable review agents and quality gates to improve consistency across pull requests.

use_cases.title: Automate PR Feedback Collection
use_cases.description: Connect GitHub Actions, review comments, labels, and metrics into a single review process.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic PR Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request 123 with the GitHub code review skill. Focus on correctness, tests, and clear feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Security Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request 123 for security issues. Prioritize authentication, authorization, secrets, injection risks, and dependency changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Multi-Agent Review Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinated review for a larger change
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a review plan for pull request 123 using security, performance, architecture, style, and accessibility agents. Include expected outputs and quality gates.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Review Automation Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate the automated review workflow for pull request 123. Check webhook safety, token scope, command validation, approval rules, and merge controls.

output_examples.input: Review PR 123 for security and performance regressions.
output: Security review summary with critical, high, and low priority findings.
Performance observations with suggested benchmarks or follow-up tests.
GitHub-ready review comments and labels for the pull request.

output_examples.input: Set up an automated review workflow for new pull requests.
output: A workflow outline for collecting PR context and running review agents.
Quality gate recommendations for security, performance, style, and architecture checks.
Operational cautions for token scope, webhook validation, and command execution.

output_examples.input: Generate a final review report for a large feature PR.
output: A concise decision summary with approval status and remaining blockers.
Grouped findings by agent type and severity.
Next actions for authors, reviewers, and release owners.

best_practices: Run commands only in trusted repositories with explicit user approval and limited GitHub token scopes.
Validate PR comments, webhook signatures, and command arguments before any automation executes.
Use the generated review as decision support and keep human approval for risky changes.
anti_patterns: Do not allow arbitrary PR comments to trigger shell commands or privileged automation.
Do not pass unreviewed model output directly into GitHub approval, merge, or labeling commands.
Do not run external npm packages with repository secrets unless the package and version are trusted.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub access?
faq.answer: Yes. Most workflows require gh CLI authentication and repository permissions for pull request data and comments.

faq.question: Can it approve or merge pull requests automatically?
faq.answer: The skill includes examples for approval and merge automation, but teams should require human review for these actions.

faq.question: Which review areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers security, performance, architecture, style, accessibility, tests, quality gates, and review metrics.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with public pull requests?
faq.answer: Use caution. Public pull requests can contain untrusted input, so tokens, webhooks, and commands need strict controls.

faq.question: Does it install or run external tools?
faq.answer: The examples use gh, npx, ruv-swarm, claude-flow, jq, npm, and shell commands. Verify each tool before use.

faq.question: Can it replace a human reviewer?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize review work and produce feedback, but human reviewers should make final decisions.
